newsitem.title: UK: ICI dollar bond spread seen in high 40s bp.
newsitem.headline: ICI dollar bond spread seen in high 40s bp.

text.p: British chemicals giant Imperial Chemical Industries Plc's planned dollar Eurobond will be a five-year offering, likely priced in the high 40s basis points over U.S. Treasuries, primary market players said on Friday.
"There is no official price talk...but I wouldn't argue against the rumour (of a spread in the high-40s b.p.)," said a syndicate manager close to the deal.
ICI, which is going through a major restructuring, on Thursday awarded Deutsche Morgan Grenfell and UBS the mandate to lead manage a benchmark dollar transaction.

Market talk was for a $500-$750 million bond, a deal which will be ICI's first public offering in international capital markets since it floated off Zeneca in 1993. Launch was expected early next week, market conditions permitting.
A syndicate manager at one of the joint leads said: "While it will be a benchmark transaction it won't be enormous," which was as much as either lead would say about the size.
Investor presentations began in London on Thursday.
The deal will begin the process of refinancing an $8.5 billion loan ICI took out in May in conjunction with its $8 billion purchase of Unilever's speciality chemicals business.
ICI last Monday pulled off its second coup in as many months with the sale of half its bulk chemical operations to U.S. chemicals giant DuPont for $3 billion.
The sale of its polyester and most of its titanium dioxide operations went some way to footing the $8 billion Unilever bill.
ICI said the sale was a "decisive step" in its goal of moving from the unpredictable world of bulk chemicals into high margin, consumer-led niches of speciality chemicals.
That line was repeated by DMG and UBS today.
"People are going to have to make a judgement as to how effective the reorganisation will be," one syndicate manager said.
ICI is rated Baa1 by Moody's and A- by S&P, having been cut from A3 in June and A+ in May respectively after the Unilever purchase.

Monday's disposal to DuPont, which follows a 100 million stg sale and leaseback deal on its London headquarters and the sale of its stake in ICI Australia, immediately cut the massive interest charges being paid by the group.
ICI has been rewarded for its efforts by the stock market, with its price at 925 pence stg at 0830 GMT from 810p before the DuPont announcement on Monday
Some analysts predicted the stock could reach 1000p over the coming weeks as it was re-rated to reflect the higher quality of earnings expected from its new product range.

But analysts warned ICI still had much to do, not least the sale of the remaining half of its bulk chemical operations which include explosives, fertilisers, chlor chemicals and the North American Tioxide business.

Analysts who have been used to criticising ICI for its ponderousness lauded the speed with which the DuPont deal had been concluded and the price achieved, saying DuPont had paid a premium for the ICI businesses.
